kjv: I saw gods ascending out of the earth
mine: I see a divine being coming up out of the earth
note: Hebrew elohim with a plural participle (olim) can mean "gods" or a single supernatural being; Saul's follow-up "What does he look like?" shows one figure is meant, so "gods" misleads. Context: a divine being (medium confidence). Saul's follow-up 'What is his appearance?' (singular) and the answer 'an old man is coming up' point to one figure, and elohim can denote a single spirit-being. But the participle 'olim is plural, so she may describe more than one figure, as LXX and Vulgate read. NASB, NRSV and NJPS read 'a divine being'. Other possible meanings: (1) 'gods' or 'divine beings coming up', more than one figure — LXX theous, Vulgate deos, KJV, some commentators from the plural participle; (2) 'a god' — ESV; (3) 'a ghostly figure' or 'spirit form', the dead as elohim (cf. Isa 8:19) — NIV, CSB.
